CHAPTER 3  
NEW IDEAS 
3.1 Introduction 
This chapter will build on the research findings from chapter 2, introducing the 
projects novel concepts, features, and scope, rationalised by key limitations and 
gaps within existing frameworks and literature. Additionally, a delineation of the 
empirical investigation, user flow and UI designs, will be made ready for 
implementation in chapter 4.  
3.2 Project Scope and Aims 
The core of this project is to create an eLearning application for GCSE science 
students, utilising short-form content delivery and interactive questions, along 
with competitive and rewards-based systems. Additionally, the project will aim 
to validate itself with empirical research around the effectiveness of these 
features at engaging and motivating students.  
The project will have a limited quantity of lessons and subjects, although it will 
be designed in such a way that the addition of lessons will be programmatically 
intuitive and highly scalable. While the project will conduct user trials and 
feedback collection, an extensive long-term study falls out of the project’s 
timeframe and scope. 
The projects timeframe is constrained by the academic calendar, enforcing a 
strict timetable to complete development, testing, and written stages. The 
budget of the project is also a limiting factor, restraining what features maybe 
implemented.
